facts.text: Abbotsford farms and agri-businesses generate $3.83 billion in economic activity, with compounded annual growth of 3.49 percent after inflation.
Abbotsford has the most productive agricultural land in Canada, and its agricultural sector generates $3.8 billion in economic activity annually.
In 2023, 1,275,484 passengers passed through Abbotsford International Airport, which surpassed the one million passenger mark for the second year in a row, a first in its history.
Abbotsford International Airport expects 2025 passenger volumes to exceed 2024 levels, with a $6 million modernization of terminal facilities among the investments planned.
Cascade Aerospace of Abbotsford is a specialty aerospace and defence contractor focused on long-term integrated aircraft support for manufacturers, military, government and commercial customers.

overview: Abbotsford had 153,524 residents in the 2021 Census, up 8.6 percent from 141,397 in 2016, making it the largest municipality in British Columbia outside Metro Vancouver. It is young for its size, with a median age of 39.2, and households earned a median of $90,000 in 2020. Its 53,234 occupied dwellings sit on 375.33 square kilometres, much of it farmland.

Agriculture, aerospace and a growing airport anchor the economy, alongside health care and retail serving the Fraser Valley. For a local business, Abbotsford combines a family-oriented, relatively prosperous customer base with a large farm and industrial sector that buys locally and values long-standing relationships.
